_readme: Each prospect gets one arm of every experiment when its offer is assigned (lib.js assignOffers, run by build.js and pitch.js), stored in prospects.json so the demo, email and replies always match. Arms are balanced until each has minPerArm pitches, then Thompson sampling sends most new pitches to the likely winner while still testing the rest. A pitch counts once it is ageDays old. learn.js retires an arm only when it has less than a 5% chance of being best after minPerArm results, adds a higher price challenger when the top price is winning, and says when a copy test needs a new challenger (the daily run writes it, following voice.md). The three tests are assigned independently, so they don't disturb each other. Never edit an arm's text after it has been sent; retire it and add a new one.

price.metric: won client (deposit or paid), weighed by first-year value: build price + expected care plan revenue

arms.text: I built a free homepage for {name}
Reply "yes" and I'll finish it in 3 days.
If you like it, reply "yes" and it can be live within 3 days of getting your photos.

format.why: Research (2026-11-15): one vendor A/B test saw a link in the first cold email cut replies from 9.4% to 5.1%; no study settles whether stating a small price up front helps. Our offer is the demo, so test it.

arms.note: demo link + price in the email (original)
no link or price: "Want me to send you the link?" (link and price go in the reply)
demo link, price only on the demo page
